Please solve this issue: The portal needs a curve instead of one usage lump for the requested window. Return each dimension in its requested steps, using clock-aligned bucket edges and clamping the first and last bucket to the window. Carry a provisioned dimension's standing level, including one last set however long before the window, through steps with no new reading, use zero for unused steps, and return every step even when the customer has no readings. Report every published group of a metadata-priced dimension separately. Readings live in the usage metrics published to CloudWatch. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

# Metering Backend

This repository serves to hold the backend infrastructure for Metering. Specifically it contains the code for the Private and Public API

### Current Status

Don't break this.
[![CI](https://github.com/example-org/metering-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/example-org/metering-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml)

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.

steps.message:
The implementation is complete. Summary of changes:

**New `src/usage/usageCurve.ts`** — the curve machinery:
- `stepsOfWindow` walks a window in **clock-aligned** edges for `hour`/`day`/`month`, **clamping the first and last step to the window** (an interval that asks for no stepping, e.g. `none`-less/undefined, leaves the window whole).
- `curveOfSteps` reduces the readings that fall into each step with the dimension's aggregation method, **returns every step**, uses **zero for unused steps**, and — when the dimension carries a standing level — **repeats the last known level** through steps holding no reading.
- `carriesStandingLevel` (provisioned = `SampleType.continious`), `latestSampleOf`, `orderSamples`, plus the shared `reduceSamples`.

**`src/usage/usageAggregation.event.ts`** — the aggregated read of the CloudWatch usage metrics now:
- builds a curve over the requested steps instead of one lump per window,
- for a provisioned dimension looks up the level the series was left standing at from the beginning of time (`START_OF_TIME`), so a level set however long before the window is carried in,
- reports zeros for every step when a customer has no published readings at all,
- reports **each published group of a metadata-priced dimension** (`tiersGroupByMetadata`) as its own `MetadataGroupedAggregatedUsageResponse` with its `metadataGroup`, while other dimensions keep a single pooled curve,
- leaves the un-aggregated (`none`) raw reading path untouched.

**`src/usage/usageCurve.spec.ts`** — unit coverage for step alignment/clamping, zero-fill, carry-forward (in-window and pre-window), per-step aggregation methods; verified end-to-end against the local AWS emulator's seeded `Metering/Usage` series (hour/day/month steps, grouped curves, carried levels, empty customers), and the existing unit suite still passes (only the pre-existing network-dependent suites fail).
